title: China-to-North Macedonia BESS Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: BESS Fire-Safety and Local Installation Review
rows.target_requirement: North Macedonia BESS projects may need municipal fire brigade review, building authority review, occupational-safety review, insurer review, and project-owner review in addition to CE-oriented product evidence. Fire expectations are generally implemented through site design, fire detection and suppression design, ventilation or gas-management, emergency shutdown, separation distances, and commissioning documentation rather than a single confirmed whole-unit national BESS fire certificate.
target_standards: North Macedonia fire code and municipal fire-safety framework
Local fire-authority, municipality, insurer, and project-owner fire-safety review
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 44240-2024, GB/T 36276-2023, GB/T 36558, and project fire-design review for stationary energy storage. These documents can support a North Macedonia fire-safety file but do not replace North Macedonia local fire-authority or site-acceptance expectations.
rows.gap: Prepare a site-specific fire dossier: cabinet layout, cell chemistry, thermal-runaway mitigation, fire detection and suppression concept, ventilation or gas-hazard analysis, spacing, access routes, emergency shutdown, water-runoff or contamination controls where relevant, commissioning tests, and North Macedonia-aligned emergency procedures.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where North Macedonia building, municipality, occupational-safety, insurer, or local fire-authority review applies; no confirmed blanket national whole-unit BESS fire certificate is stated here
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or project-specific depending on Chinese project approval, local fire review, and procurement requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Product safety evidence alone is not enough for North Macedonia BESS fire review. Treat fire design and local installation acceptance as project-specific approval items.

source.publisher: Government of North Macedonia, State fire-safety and municipal authorities

rows.requirement: ERC and MEPSO Grid-Connection and Market Participation Review
rows.target_requirement: North Macedonia reviews storage projects through the Energy Regulatory Commission and MEPSO according to connection point, installed capacity, market role, and balancing-route method. For North Macedonia-facing BESS documents, provide ERC activity classification, interconnection agreement route, interconnection agreement documents, grid-study outputs, metering, protection-coordination evidence, dispatch interfaces, commissioning evidence, and site commissioning records before energisation.
target_standards: North Macedonia electricity law and storage market implementation procedures administered by ERC
MEPSO interconnection, grid-code, and operating practice at the project connection point
IEC 62933-5-2 for internationally expected grid-integrated BESS evidence where project rules require
rows.china_equivalent: China often uses GB/T 36558-2023 and related utility procedures for project grid studies and integration planning of electrochemical energy storage. These materials can support technical comparison but do not replace ERC / MEPSO approval or project interconnection decisions.
china_standards: China grid-company interconnection and acceptance requirements
rows.gap: The key gap is the North Macedonia project pathway. Exporters should confirm whether BESS is treated as storage, embedded generation, or capacity resource by ERC and MEPSO, and map protection settings, islanding logic, import current limits, voltage regulation settings, and operating interfaces before project acceptance.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where North Macedonia projects require ERC status definition, MEPSO interconnection documentation, or market-participation authorization
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — China GB/T project evidence is not North Macedonia ERC/MEPSO grid-approval proof

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep grid interconnection, dispatch participation, and market activity pathways separate from product safety documents. North Macedonia project approvals require route-specific ERC and MEPSO checks even if technical evidence is complete.

rows.requirement: CE-Aligned Electrical Safety and BESS Standards
rows.target_requirement: North Macedonia applies EU-CE candidate alignment for in-scope electrical products through ISRSM and market adoption channels. For lithium-ion BESS, IEC 62619 baseline is commonly expected for battery safety and IEC 62933-5-2 for system safety evidence in grid-connected installations. Exporters should map model scope, voltage class, and country pathway before shipment.
target_standards: North Macedonia CE-oriented electrical safety implementation via ISRSM
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB 44240-2024 and GB/T 36276-2023 for energy-storage lithium safety, and GB/T 36558 for system integration evidence. Those reports support technical comparison but do not substitute for North Macedonia-facing EN-aligned or project-specific evidence.
rows.gap: Do not assume Chinese GB battery safety evidence is sufficient for North Macedonia filing. Prepare EN/IEC evidence aligned to North Macedonia-facing scope, including voltage class, thermal-management assumptions, isolation and protection design, risk analysis, and model-level declaration controls.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for in-scope electrical equipment when North Macedonia market and project docs require CE-aligned EN/IEC evidence
mandatory_status.cn: Not a direct substitute for North Macedonia market placement or project acceptance requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Maintain a North Macedonia-facing EN/IEC evidence pack rather than reusing China domestic battery safety reports as final placement readiness proof.

source.publisher: Standardization Institute of the Republic of North Macedonia (ISRSM); IEC

rows.requirement: Lithium Battery Transport — UN 38.3 and Dangerous-Goods Documentation
rows.target_requirement: Lithium-ion cells and batteries shipped to North Macedonia normally need UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, subsection 38.3 transport test evidence and the related test summary before air, sea, road, or multimodal transport. North Macedonia transport compliance is separate from CE product conformity, ERC requirements, and MEPSO connection approval.
target_standards: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, subsection 38.3
UN Model Regulations dangerous-goods framework for lithium batteries
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese exporters often hold UN 38.3 reports and transport-condition documentation for outbound lithium-battery shipments. These documents can support North Macedonia-bound shipment planning, but the shipper must still match the exact cell, battery, module, state of charge, packaging, dangerous-goods declaration, and modal transport rules for the actual route.
china_standards: UN 38.3 test report and lithium-battery transport summary
China outbound dangerous-goods transport documentation for lithium batteries
rows.gap: A BESS safety certificate does not satisfy dangerous-goods transport documentation. Exporters should prepare model-specific UN 38.3 reports, test summaries, SDS, packing instructions, battery net mass information, state-of-charge controls, and carrier-required declarations for the selected route to North Macedonia.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for regulated lithium-battery transport where UN dangerous-goods rules are incorporated by selected mode and route
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for regulated outbound lithium-battery transport documentation; not a substitute for destination product or grid approval

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] UN 38.3 is a shipment gate, not North Macedonia market approval. Match the transport test summary and dangerous-goods package to the exact shipped battery configuration and transport route.

source.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE)
